input.summary:
P1 hall NOT lit: parts/room-9.mjs now writes two hanging lanterns at (23,4,16) and (23,4,19) from the y5 ceiling, but runParts refuses both because the shell locked every hall cell as air. The hall is at min 1, mean 5.4, 0 dark and 22 of 28 floor cells dim (1-7), so the 8+ target is not met.
make.sh still produces a whole build.nbt, and the shell, stairs and other parts are unchanged.
The lanterns will land once the lock lets room cells in or the shell stops locking the hall's air; I did not bypass the lock or edit the shell.
left: P1 hall has no light yet: the two hanging lanterns at (23,4,16) and (23,4,19) (the last lines of parts/room-9.mjs build(g)) are refused by runParts with 'REFUSED 2 writes into earlier parts ... 23,4,16 lantern air'. The shell (Part 1) carves every hall cell to air and the lock covers air too, so no room part can place a lamp in the hall as written.

Current light in the hall: min 1, mean 5.4, 0 dark, 22 of 28 floor cells dim (1-7). Target is 8+ on every floor cell, so the hall still fails `mcd room --only "P1 hall"`. The tool's own suggestion (a standing lantern at 22,2,14) is also inside locked air.

Decision for the architect or the lock owner (not mine to change): either let room parts write lamps into shell air in the hall (for example, lock only solid cells, or exempt lamp states), or have the shell leave the hall's ceiling-anchor cells unlocked. Any fix that makes the two lanterns land should then be re-checked with `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P1 hall"`.

Other refusals in the same build, not from this part: the glazing part has 230 refused writes at the front windows (air locked by the shell), and room P3 dining room has 9 refused writes. These are outside the lamplighter's scope and were left alone.

waste.what: Checked the P1 hall light by hand after each rebuild: ran make.sh, then the room check, then the light command, and read the refused-write lines in the build log to see why the lanterns did not land.
waste.cost: 3 full make.sh rebuilds (about 11,500 cells each) plus 2 room/light checks.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --lamp-test x,y,z,lantern` or a dry-run that reports which proposed lamp cells the runParts lock would refuse, before a full rebuild, and tells whether the lamp is locked by shell air, a wall or the stair joiner.

waste.what: Worked out lantern positions by hand from the room box and the floor-to-ceiling layout (y4 under the y5 floor block, centre line x23, z16 and z19) instead of asking the tool for lamp cells the lock would accept.
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate checks against the room map, no blocks placed beyond the two lanterns.
waste.tool: `mcd room --only "<room>" --free-cells` listing the cells in the room box that no earlier part owns, so the lamplighter sees the usable lamp spots at once.

companions.task: Decide the lock rule for the hall: whether room parts may place lamps into shell air (lock solid cells only, or exempt lantern states), or whether the shell should leave the hall's ceiling-anchor cells unlocked. Owns plan.md and the Part 1 shell.
Once the lock allows it, re-run make.sh and `mcd room --only "P1 hall"` to confirm the two hanging lanterns clear the 8+ target with no dark cell, and adjust position only if a dim cell remains.
